## `crates/forge-core/src/ingest/text.rs`

```rust
//! Text-family adapters: plain text, markdown, HTML and CSV/TSV.
//!
//! HTML is parsed with a small, dependency-free tokeniser that drops script/style
//! content, decodes the common entities and keeps heading context. It is not a
//! full HTML5 parser and does not execute or render anything.

use super::Block;
use crate::domain::Locator;

fn push_paragraph(out: &mut Vec<Block>, idx: &mut u32, text: &str, section: Option<String>) {
    let trimmed = text.trim();
    if trimmed.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let mut loc = Locator::paragraph(*idx, 0, trimmed.len() as u32);
    loc.section = section;
    out.push(Block { text: trimmed.to_string(), locator: loc });
    *idx += 1;
}

pub fn plain_blocks(raw: &str) -> Vec<Block> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut idx = 0u32;
    let mut current = String::new();
    for line in raw.lines() {
        if line.trim().is_empty() {
            push_paragraph(&mut out, &mut idx, &current, None);
            current.clear();
        } else {
            if !current.is_empty() {
                current.push(' ');
            }
            current.push_str(line.trim());
        }
    }
    push_paragraph(&mut out, &mut idx, &current, None);
    out
}

pub fn markdown_blocks(raw: &str) -> Vec<Block> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut idx = 0u32;
    let mut current = String::new();
    let mut section: Option<String> = None;
    let mut in_code = false;

    for line in raw.lines() {
        let t = line.trim();
        if t.starts_with("```") {
            in_code = !in_code;
            continue;
        }
        if !in_code {
            if let Some(rest) = t.strip_prefix('#') {
                let title = rest.trim_start_matches('#').trim();
                if !title.is_empty() {
                    push_paragraph(&mut out, &mut idx, &current, section.clone());
                    current.clear();
                    section = Some(title.to_string());
                    // headings are themselves useful evidence
                    push_paragraph(&mut out, &mut idx, title, section.clone());
                    continue;
                }
            }
            if t.is_empty() {
                push_paragraph(&mut out, &mut idx, &current, section.clone());
                current.clear();
                continue;
            }
            // list items become their own evidence units
            if t.starts_with("- ") || t.starts_with("* ") || t.starts_with("+ ") {
                push_paragraph(&mut out, &mut idx, &current, section.clone());
                current.clear();
                push_paragraph(&mut out, &mut idx, &t[2..], section.clone());
                continue;
            }
        }
        if !current.is_empty() {
            current.push(' ');
        }
        current.push_str(t);
    }
    push_paragraph(&mut out, &mut idx, &current, section);
    out
}

pub fn html_blocks(raw: &str) -> (Vec<Block>, Vec<String>) {
    let mut warnings = Vec::new();
    let mut text = String::new();
    let mut sections: Vec<Block> = Vec::new();
    let mut idx = 0u32;
    let mut skip_depth = 0usize; // inside script/style
    let mut current_section: Option<String> = None;
    let mut chars = raw.char_indices().peekable();

    while let Some((i, c)) = chars.next() {
        if c == '<' {
            // read tag
            let mut tag = String::new();
            for (_, c2) in chars.by_ref() {
                if c2 == '>' {
                    break;
                }
                tag.push(c2);
            }
            let t = tag.trim().trim_start_matches('/').to_ascii_lowercase();
            let name: String = t
                .split(|ch: char| ch.is_whitespace() || ch == '/')
                .next()
                .unwrap_or("")
                .to_string();
            let closing = tag.trim_start().starts_with('/');
            if name == "script" || name == "style" {
                if closing {
                    skip_depth = skip_depth.saturating_sub(1);
                } else if !tag.trim_end().ends_with('/') {
                    skip_depth += 1;
                }
                continue;
            }
            if skip_depth > 0 {
                continue;
            }
            match name.as_str() {
                "p" | "div" | "br" | "li" | "tr" | "section" | "article" | "blockquote" | "pre" => {
                    text.push('\n');
                }
                "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "h5" | "h6" => {
                    text.push('\n');
                    if !closing {
                        // capture the heading text that follows
                        let mut head = String::new();
                        for (_, c2) in chars.by_ref() {
                            if c2 == '<' {
                                break;
                            }
                            head.push(c2);
                        }
                        let head = decode_entities(&head).trim().to_string();
                        if !head.is_empty() {
                            current_section = Some(head.clone());
                            push_paragraph(&mut sections, &mut idx, &head, None);
                        }
                    }
                }
                "img" => {
                    if let Some(alt) = attr(&tag, "alt") {
                        if !alt.trim().is_empty() {
                            text.push(' ');
                            text.push_str(&alt);
                        }
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
            let _ = i;
            continue;
        }
        if skip_depth == 0 {
            text.push(c);
        }
    }

    let decoded = decode_entities(&text);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut idx2 = 0u32;
    for line in decoded.lines() {
        let t = line.trim();
        if t.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let mut loc = Locator::paragraph(idx2, 0, t.len() as u32);
        loc.section = current_section.clone();
        out.push(Block { text: t.to_string(), locator: loc });
        idx2 += 1;
    }
    out.extend(sections);
    if out.is_empty() {
        warnings.push("no readable text found in HTML (script-only page?)".into());
    }
    (out, warnings)
}

fn attr(tag: &str, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let lower = tag.to_ascii_lowercase();
    let at = lower.find(&format!("{}=", name))?;
    let rest = &tag[at + name.len() + 1..];
    let quote = rest.chars().next()?;
    if quote == '"' || quote == '\'' {
        let end = rest[1..].find(quote)?;
        Some(decode_entities(&rest[1..1 + end]))
    } else {
        let end = rest.find(|c: char| c.is_whitespace()).unwrap_or(rest.len());
        Some(rest[..end].to_string())
    }
}

pub fn decode_entities(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut rest = s;
    while let Some(pos) = rest.find('&') {
        out.push_str(&rest[..pos]);
        let tail = &rest[pos..];
        if let Some(semi) = tail[..tail.len().min(12)].find(';') {
            let entity = &tail[1..semi];
            let replacement = match entity {
                "amp" => Some('&'),
                "lt" => Some('<'),
                "gt" => Some('>'),
                "quot" => Some('"'),
                "apos" => Some('\''),
                "nbsp" => Some(' '),
                "mdash" => Some('—'),
                "ndash" => Some('–'),
                "hellip" => Some('…'),
                _ => {
                    if let Some(num) = entity.strip_prefix("#x").or_else(|| entity.strip_prefix("#X")) {
                        u32::from_str_radix(num, 16).ok().and_then(char::from_u32)
                    } else if let Some(num) = entity.strip_prefix('#') {
                        num.parse::<u32>().ok().and_then(char::from_u32)
                    } else {
                        None
                    }
                }
            };
            match replacement {
                Some(c) => {
                    out.push(c);
                    rest = &tail[semi + 1..];
                }
                None => {
                    out.push('&');
                    rest = &tail[1..];
                }
            }
        } else {
            out.push('&');
            rest = &tail[1..];
        }
    }
    out.push_str(rest);
    out
}

/// CSV/TSV: one block per row, keeping the header as a prefix so a row is
/// self-describing when retrieved on its own.
pub fn csv_blocks(raw: &str, tsv: bool) -> (Vec<Block>, Vec<String>) {
    let mut warnings = Vec::new();
    let delim = if tsv { '\t' } else { ',' };
    let rows = parse_csv(raw, delim);
    if rows.is_empty() {
        return (Vec::new(), vec!["empty CSV".into()]);
    }
    let header = rows[0].clone();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for (i, row) in rows.iter().enumerate().skip(1) {
        let mut parts = Vec::new();
        for (ci, cell) in row.iter().enumerate() {
            let name = header.get(ci).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| format!("col{}", ci + 1));
            let value = cell.trim();
            if !value.is_empty() {
                parts.push(format!("{}: {}", name.trim(), value));
            }
        }
        if parts.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let text = parts.join(" | ");
        let mut loc = Locator::row(i as u32, 0, text.len() as u32);
        loc.section = Some(header.join(" | "));
        out.push(Block { text, locator: loc });
    }
    if rows.len() == 1 {
        warnings.push("CSV had a header but no data rows".into());
    }
    (out, warnings)
}

fn parse_csv(raw: &str, delim: char) -> Vec<Vec<String>> {
    let mut rows = Vec::new();
    let mut row = Vec::new();
    let mut cell = String::new();
    let mut in_quotes = false;
    let mut chars = raw.chars().peekable();
    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
        if in_quotes {
            if c == '"' {
                if chars.peek() == Some(&'"') {
                    cell.push('"');
                    chars.next();
                } else {
                    in_quotes = false;
                }
            } else {
                cell.push(c);
            }
        } else if c == '"' {
            in_quotes = true;
        } else if c == delim {
            row.push(std::mem::take(&mut cell));
        } else if c == '\n' {
            row.push(std::mem::take(&mut cell));
            rows.push(std::mem::take(&mut row));
        } else if c == '\r' {
            // ignore
        } else {
            cell.push(c);
        }
    }
    if !cell.is_empty() || !row.is_empty() {
        row.push(cell);
        rows.push(row);
    }
    rows.retain(|r| !(r.len() == 1 && r[0].trim().is_empty()));
    rows
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn plain_text_paragraphs() {
        let blocks = plain_blocks("First para.\nStill first.\n\nSecond para.\n");
        assert_eq!(blocks.len(), 2);
        assert!(blocks[0].text.contains("Still first"));
        assert_eq!(blocks[0].locator.paragraph, Some(0));
        assert_eq!(blocks[1].locator.paragraph, Some(1));
    }

    #[test]
    fn markdown_sections_and_lists() {
        let md = "# Intro\n\nSome text.\n\n- bullet one\n- bullet two\n\n## Detail\nMore detail.\n";
        let blocks = markdown_blocks(md);
        let texts: Vec<&str> = blocks.iter().map(|b| b.text.as_str()).collect();
        assert!(texts.contains(&"Intro"));
        assert!(texts.contains(&"bullet one"));
        assert!(texts.iter().any(|t| t.contains("More detail")));
        assert!(blocks.iter().any(|b| b.locator.section.as_deref() == Some("Detail")));
    }

    #[test]
    fn html_strips_scripts_and_decodes_entities() {
        let html = "<html><head><style>body{color:red}</style><script>var x=1;</script></head>\
                    <body><h1>Title</h1><p>Tom &amp; Jerry &lt;3</p><p>Caf&#233;</p></body></html>";
        let (blocks, warnings) = html_blocks(html);
        let joined: String = blocks.iter().map(|b| b.text.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ");
        assert!(!joined.contains("var x"));
        assert!(!joined.contains("color:red"));
        assert!(joined.contains("Tom & Jerry <3"));
        assert!(joined.contains("Café"));
        assert!(blocks.iter().any(|b| b.locator.section.as_deref() == Some("Title")));
        assert!(warnings.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn csv_rows_are_self_describing() {
        let csv = "name,score\nAda,95\nGrace,88\n";
        let (blocks, _) = csv_blocks(csv, false);
        assert_eq!(blocks.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(blocks[0].text, "name: Ada | score: 95");
        assert_eq!(blocks[0].locator.row, Some(1));
    }

    #[test]
    fn csv_handles_quotes_and_commas() {
        let csv = "title,note\n\"Hello, world\",\"He said \"\"hi\"\"\"\n";
        let (blocks, _) = csv_blocks(csv, false);
        assert_eq!(blocks[0].text, "title: Hello, world | note: He said \"hi\"");
    }

    #[test]
    fn entities_and_numeric_refs() {
        assert_eq!(decode_entities("a&amp;b&#65;&#x42;&nbsp;c"), "a&bAB c");
        assert_eq!(decode_entities("100% &unknown;"), "100% &unknown;");
    }
}

## `crates/forge-core/src/ingest/zip.rs`

```rust
//! Minimal ZIP reader (enough for OOXML/EPUB): central directory + stored/deflated entries.
//!
//! Only what the format needs: no encryption, no ZIP64, no multi-disk. Anything
//! outside that returns a clear error instead of silently producing garbage.

pub struct Entry {
    pub name: String,
    pub compressed_size: u64,
    pub uncompressed_size: u64,
    pub method: u16,
    pub local_offset: u64,
}

fn u16le(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    Some(u16::from_le_bytes([*b.get(at)?, *b.get(at + 1)?]))
}

fn u32le(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    Some(u32::from_le_bytes([
        *b.get(at)?,
        *b.get(at + 1)?,
        *b.get(at + 2)?,
        *b.get(at + 3)?,
    ]))
}

const EOCD: u32 = 0x0605_4b50;
const CEN: u32 = 0x0201_4b50;
const LOC: u32 = 0x0403_4b50;

/// Locate and parse the central directory.
pub fn entries(data: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Entry>, String> {
    if data.len() < 22 {
        return Err("zip: file too small".into());
    }
    // The EOCD record is at the end; the comment may be up to 65535 bytes.
    let mut eocd = None;
    let start = data.len().saturating_sub(65557);
    let mut i = data.len().saturating_sub(22);
    loop {
        if u32le(data, i) == Some(EOCD) {
            eocd = Some(i);
            break;
        }
        if i == start {
            break;
        }
        i -= 1;
    }
    let eocd = eocd.ok_or_else(|| "zip: end-of-central-directory record not found".to_string())?;

    let count = u16le(data, eocd + 10).ok_or("zip: truncated EOCD")? as usize;
    let cd_size = u32le(data, eocd + 12).ok_or("zip: truncated EOCD")? as usize;
    let cd_off = u32le(data, eocd + 16).ok_or("zip: truncated EOCD")? as usize;
    if cd_off == 0xFFFF_FFFF || count == 0xFFFF {
        return Err("zip: ZIP64 archives are not supported".into());
    }
    if cd_off.saturating_add(cd_size) > data.len() {
        return Err("zip: central directory out of bounds".into());
    }

    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(count);
    let mut p = cd_off;
    for _ in 0..count {
        if u32le(data, p) != Some(CEN) {
            return Err("zip: bad central directory entry".into());
        }
        let method = u16le(data, p + 10).ok_or("zip: truncated entry")?;
        let compressed_size = u32le(data, p + 20).ok_or("zip: truncated entry")? as u64;
        let uncompressed_size = u32le(data, p + 24).ok_or("zip: truncated entry")? as u64;
        let name_len = u16le(data, p + 28).ok_or("zip: truncated entry")? as usize;
        let extra_len = u16le(data, p + 30).ok_or("zip: truncated entry")? as usize;
        let comment_len = u16le(data, p + 32).ok_or("zip: truncated entry")? as usize;
        let local_offset = u32le(data, p + 42).ok_or("zip: truncated entry")? as u64;
        let name_bytes = data
            .get(p + 46..p + 46 + name_len)
            .ok_or("zip: entry name out of bounds")?;
        let name = String::from_utf8_lossy(name_bytes).to_string();
        out.push(Entry {
            name,
            compressed_size,
            uncompressed_size,
            method,
            local_offset,
        });
        p += 46 + name_len + extra_len + comment_len;
    }
    Ok(out)
}

pub fn read(data: &[u8], entry: &Entry) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let at = entry.local_offset as usize;
    if u32le(data, at) != Some(LOC) {
        return Err(format!("zip: bad local header for {}", entry.name));
    }
    let name_len = u16le(data, at + 26).ok_or("zip: truncated local header")? as usize;
    let extra_len = u16le(data, at + 28).ok_or("zip: truncated local header")? as usize;
    let data_start = at + 30 + name_len + extra_len;
    let end = data_start + entry.compressed_size as usize;
    let raw = data
        .get(data_start..end)
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("zip: data out of bounds for {}", entry.name))?;
    match entry.method {
        0 => Ok(raw.to_vec()),
        8 => crate::inflate::inflate_raw(raw)
            .map_err(|e| format!("zip: deflate failed for {}: {}", entry.name, e)),
        m => Err(format!("zip: compression method {} is not supported", m)),
    }
}

/// Read an entry by exact name.
pub fn read_named(data: &[u8], name: &str) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, String> {
    let all = entries(data)?;
    match all.iter().find(|e| e.name == name) {
        None => Ok(None),
        Some(e) => read(data, e).map(Some),
    }
}

/// Find entries whose name starts with `prefix` and ends with `suffix`.
pub fn find(data: &[u8], prefix: &str, suffix: &str) -> Result<Vec<Entry>, String> {
    Ok(entries(data)?
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|e| e.name.starts_with(prefix) && e.name.ends_with(suffix))
        .collect())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::inflate;

    #[test]
    fn reads_stored_and_deflated_entries() {
        let path = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
            .join("../../tests/fixtures/sample.docx");
        let data = std::fs::read(&path).expect("fixture sample.docx missing");
        let doc = read_named(&data, "word/document.xml").unwrap().expect("document.xml");
        let xml = String::from_utf8_lossy(&doc);
        assert!(xml.contains("<w:t"), "stored entry text");
        let styles = read_named(&data, "word/styles.xml").unwrap().expect("styles.xml");
        assert!(styles.len() > 50, "deflated entry expanded");
        assert!(read_named(&data, "word/nope.xml").unwrap().is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_non_zip_and_garbage() {
        assert!(entries(b"plain text, definitely not a zip").is_err());
        assert!(inflate::inflate_raw(b"garbage").is_err());
    }
}
```

## `crates/forge-core/src/json.rs`

```rust
//! Minimal, strict JSON implementation (no external crates are available:
//! crates.io is unreachable in this environment, see docs/DECISIONS.md D1).
//!
//! Supports: objects, arrays, strings with escapes, numbers, booleans, null.
//! Rejects trailing garbage and unescaped control characters.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::fmt::Write as _;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Value {
    Null,
    Bool(bool),
    Num(f64),
    Str(String),
    Arr(Vec<Value>),
    Obj(BTreeMap<String, Value>),
}

impl Value {
    pub fn obj() -> Value {
        Value::Obj(BTreeMap::new())
    }

    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&Value> {
        match self {
            Value::Obj(m) => m.get(key),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn str_of(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        match self.get(key) {
            Some(Value::Str(s)) => Some(s.as_str()),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn as_str(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        match self {
            Value::Str(s) => Some(s),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn as_f64(&self) -> Option<f64> {
        match self {
            Value::Num(n) => Some(*n),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn as_bool(&self) -> Option<bool> {
        match self {
            Value::Bool(b) => Some(*b),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn as_arr(&self) -> Option<&Vec<Value>> {
        match self {
            Value::Arr(a) => Some(a),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn as_obj(&self) -> Option<&BTreeMap<String, Value>> {
        match self {
            Value::Obj(m) => Some(m),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn is_null(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Value::Null)
    }
}

/// Convenience constructors so handlers read cleanly.
impl From<&str> for Value {
    fn from(s: &str) -> Self {
        Value::Str(s.to_string())
    }
}
impl From<String> for Value {
    fn from(s: String) -> Self {
        Value::Str(s)
    }
}
impl From<bool> for Value {
    fn from(b: bool) -> Self {
        Value::Bool(b)
    }
}
impl From<f64> for Value {
    fn from(n: f64) -> Self {
        Value::Num(n)
    }
}
impl From<u64> for Value {
    fn from(n: u64) -> Self {
        Value::Num(n as f64)
    }
}
impl From<usize> for Value {
    fn from(n: usize) -> Self {
        Value::Num(n as f64)
    }
}
impl From<i64> for Value {
    fn from(n: i64) -> Self {
        Value::Num(n as f64)
    }
}
impl<T: Into<Value>> From<Vec<T>> for Value {
    fn from(v: Vec<T>) -> Self {
        Value::Arr(v.into_iter().map(Into::into).collect())
    }
}

/// Builder helper for objects: `obj!{"a" => 1, "b" => "x"}`
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! obj {
    () => { $crate::json::Value::obj() };
    ($($k:expr => $v:expr),* $(,)?) => {{
        let mut m = ::std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
        $( m.insert($k.to_string(), $crate::json::Value::from($v)); )*
        $crate::json::Value::Obj(m)
    }};
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- parsing

pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
    let mut p = Parser { b: text.as_bytes(), i: 0 };
    p.ws();
    let v = p.value()?;
    p.ws();
    if p.i != p.b.len() {
        return Err(format!("trailing data at byte {}", p.i));
    }
    Ok(v)
}

struct Parser<'a> {
    b: &'a [u8],
    i: usize,
}

impl<'a> Parser<'a> {
    fn ws(&mut self) {
        while self.i < self.b.len() && matches!(self.b[self.i], b' ' | b'\t' | b'\n' | b'\r') {
            self.i += 1;
        }
    }

    fn peek(&self) -> Option<u8> {
        self.b.get(self.i).copied()
    }

    fn expect(&mut self, c: u8) -> Result<(), String> {
        if self.peek() == Some(c) {
            self.i += 1;
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(format!("expected '{}' at byte {}", c as char, self.i))
        }
    }

    fn value(&mut self) -> Result<Value, String> {
        match self.peek() {
            None => Err("unexpected end of input".into()),
            Some(b'{') => self.object(),
            Some(b'[') => self.array(),
            Some(b'"') => Ok(Value::Str(self.string()?)),
            Some(b't') => self.literal("true", Value::Bool(true)),
            Some(b'f') => self.literal("false", Value::Bool(false)),
            Some(b'n') => self.literal("null", Value::Null),
            Some(c) if c == b'-' || c.is_ascii_digit() => self.number(),
            Some(c) => Err(format!("unexpected byte '{}' at {}", c as char, self.i)),
        }
    }

    fn literal(&mut self, word: &str, v: Value) -> Result<Value, String> {
        if self.b[self.i..].starts_with(word.as_bytes()) {
            self.i += word.len();
            Ok(v)
        } else {
            Err(format!("invalid literal at byte {}", self.i))
        }
    }

    fn number(&mut self) -> Result<Value, String> {
        let start = self.i;
        if self.peek() == Some(b'-') {
            self.i += 1;
        }
        while matches!(self.peek(), Some(c) if c.is_ascii_digit()) {
            self.i += 1;
        }
        if self.peek() == Some(b'.') {
            self.i += 1;
            while matches!(self.peek(), Some(c) if c.is_ascii_digit()) {
                self.i += 1;
            }
        }
        if matches!(self.peek(), Some(b'e') | Some(b'E')) {
            self.i += 1;
            if matches!(self.peek(), Some(b'+') | Some(b'-')) {
                self.i += 1;
            }
            while matches!(self.peek(), Some(c) if c.is_ascii_digit()) {
                self.i += 1;
            }
        }
        let s = std::str::from_utf8(&self.b[start..self.i]).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        s.parse::<f64>()
            .map(Value::Num)
            .map_err(|_| format!("invalid number {:?}", s))
    }

    fn string(&mut self) -> Result<String, String> {
        self.expect(b'"')?;
        let mut out = String::new();
        loop {
            let c = self.peek().ok_or("unterminated string")?;
            self.i += 1;
            match c {
                b'"' => return Ok(out),
                b'\\' => {
                    let e = self.peek().ok_or("unterminated escape")?;
                    self.i += 1;
                    match e {
                        b'"' => out.push('"'),
                        b'\\' => out.push('\\'),
                        b'/' => out.push('/'),
                        b'b' => out.push('\u{8}'),
                        b'f' => out.push('\u{c}'),
                        b'n' => out.push('\n'),
                        b'r' => out.push('\r'),
                        b't' => out.push('\t'),
                        b'u' => {
                            let cp = self.hex4()?;
                            if (0xD800..0xDC00).contains(&cp) {
                                // high surrogate: expect a following \uXXXX low surrogate
                                if self.peek() == Some(b'\\') && self.b.get(self.i + 1) == Some(&b'u') {
                                    self.i += 2;
                                    let lo = self.hex4()?;
                                    if (0xDC00..0xE000).contains(&lo) {
                                        let c = 0x10000 + ((cp - 0xD800) << 10) + (lo - 0xDC00);
                                        out.push(char::from_u32(c).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'));
                                    } else {
                                        out.push('\u{FFFD}');
                                    }
                                } else {
                                    out.push('\u{FFFD}');
                                }
                            } else {
                                out.push(char::from_u32(cp).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'));
                            }
                        }
                        other => return Err(format!("bad escape \\{}", other as char)),
                    }
                }
                c if c < 0x20 => return Err("unescaped control character in string".into()),
                c => {
                    // Re-decode UTF-8 sequences copied byte by byte.
                    let start = self.i - 1;
                    let width = utf8_width(c);
                    if width > 1 {
                        self.i = start + width;
                    }
                    let slice = &self.b[start..self.i.min(self.b.len())];
                    out.push_str(&String::from_utf8_lossy(slice));
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn hex4(&mut self) -> Result<u32, String> {
        if self.i + 4 > self.b.len() {
            return Err("short \\u escape".into());
        }
        let s = std::str::from_utf8(&self.b[self.i..self.i + 4]).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let v = u32::from_str_radix(s, 16).map_err(|_| "bad \\u escape".to_string())?;
        self.i += 4;
        Ok(v)
    }

    fn array(&mut self) -> Result<Value, String> {
        self.expect(b'[')?;
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        self.ws();
        if self.peek() == Some(b']') {
            self.i += 1;
            return Ok(Value::Arr(out));
        }
        loop {
            self.ws();
            out.push(self.value()?);
            self.ws();
            match self.peek() {
                Some(b',') => {
                    self.i += 1;
                }
                Some(b']') => {
                    self.i += 1;
                    return Ok(Value::Arr(out));
                }
                _ => return Err(format!("expected ',' or ']' at byte {}", self.i)),
            }
        }
    }

    fn object(&mut self) -> Result<Value, String> {
        self.expect(b'{')?;
        let mut map = BTreeMap::new();
        self.ws();
        if self.peek() == Some(b'}') {
            self.i += 1;
            return Ok(Value::Obj(map));
        }
        loop {
            self.ws();
            let key = self.string()?;
            self.ws();
            self.expect(b':')?;
            self.ws();
            let val = self.value()?;
            map.insert(key, val);
            self.ws();
            match self.peek() {
                Some(b',') => {
                    self.i += 1;
                }
                Some(b'}') => {
                    self.i += 1;
                    return Ok(Value::Obj(map));
                }
                _ => return Err(format!("expected ',' or '}}' at byte {}", self.i)),
            }
        }
    }
}

fn utf8_width(b: u8) -> usize {
    if b < 0x80 {
        1
    } else if b >> 5 == 0b110 {
        2
    } else if b >> 4 == 0b1110 {
        3
    } else if b >> 3 == 0b11110 {
        4
    } else {
        1
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------ serialising

pub fn to_string(v: &Value) -> String {
    let mut s = String::new();
    write_value(&mut s, v);
    s
}

pub fn to_pretty(v: &Value) -> String {
    let mut s = String::new();
    write_pretty(&mut s, v, 0);
    s
}

fn write_value(out: &mut String, v: &Value) {
    match v {
        Value::Null => out.push_str("null"),
        Value::Bool(b) => out.push_str(if *b { "true" } else { "false" }),
        Value::Num(n) => {
            if n.is_finite() {
                if n.fract() == 0.0 && n.abs() < 9.007_199_254_740_992e15 {
                    let _ = write!(out, "{}", *n as i64);
                } else {
                    let _ = write!(out, "{}", n);
                }
            } else {
                out.push_str("null");
            }
        }
        Value::Str(s) => write_string(out, s),
        Value::Arr(items) => {
            out.push('[');
            for (i, item) in items.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                write_value(out, item);
            }
            out.push(']');
        }
        Value::Obj(map) => {
            out.push('{');
            for (i, (k, item)) in map.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                write_string(out, k);
                out.push(':');
                write_value(out, item);
            }
            out.push('}');
        }
    }
}

fn write_pretty(out: &mut String, v: &Value, depth: usize) {
    let pad = |out: &mut String, d: usize| {
        out.push('\n');
        for _ in 0..d {
            out.push_str("  ");
        }
    };
    match v {
        Value::Arr(items) if !items.is_empty() => {
            out.push('[');
            for (i, item) in items.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                pad(out, depth + 1);
                write_pretty(out, item, depth + 1);
            }
            pad(out, depth);
            out.push(']');
        }
        Value::Obj(map) if !map.is_empty() => {
            out.push('{');
            for (i, (k, item)) in map.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                pad(out, depth + 1);
                write_string(out, k);
                out.push_str(": ");
                write_pretty(out, item, depth + 1);
            }
            pad(out, depth);
            out.push('}');
        }
        other => write_value(out, other),
    }
}

fn write_string(out: &mut String, s: &str) {
    out.push('"');
    for ch in s.chars() {
        match ch {
            '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => {
                let _ = write!(out, "\\u{:04x}", c as u32);
            }
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out.push('"');
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn roundtrip_primitives() {
        let src = r#"{"a":1,"b":[true,false,null],"c":"x\"y","d":-2.5}"#;
        let v = parse(src).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(to_string(&v), r#"{"a":1,"b":[true,false,null],"c":"x\"y","d":-2.5}"#);
    }

    #[test]
    fn unicode_escapes() {
        let v = parse(r#""caf\u00e9""#).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v.as_str().unwrap(), "café");
        let v = parse(r#""\ud83d\ude00""#).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v.as_str().unwrap(), "😀");
    }

    #[test]
    fn utf8_passthrough() {
        let v = parse("{\"t\":\"日本語 café\"}").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v.str_of("t").unwrap(), "日本語 café");
        assert_eq!(parse(&to_string(&v)).unwrap(), v);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_bad_input() {
        assert!(parse("{").is_err());
        assert!(parse("{}x").is_err());
        assert!(parse("[1,]").is_err());
        assert!(parse("{\"a\" 1}").is_err());
        assert!(parse("\"unterminated").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn nested_and_empty() {
        let v = parse(r#"{"a":{},"b":[],"c":{"d":{"e":[1]}}}"#).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v.get("a").unwrap(), &Value::Obj(BTreeMap::new()));
        assert_eq!(v.get("b").unwrap(), &Value::Arr(vec![]));
        assert_eq!(to_string(&v), r#"{"a":{},"b":[],"c":{"d":{"e":[1]}}}"#);
    }

    #[test]
    fn numbers() {
        assert_eq!(parse("1e3").unwrap().as_f64().unwrap(), 1000.0);
        assert_eq!(to_string(&Value::Num(3.0)), "3");
        assert_eq!(to_string(&Value::Num(3.25)), "3.25");
    }
}

## `crates/forge-core/src/providers.rs`

```rust
//! Model-provider seam (bring-your-own-key) and the always-available local engine.
//!
//! Design contract:
//! * `Answerer` is the only way answers are produced.
//! * The **extractive** answerer always exists and needs no key or network.
//! * A remote provider can be *configured*, but it is only *used* when it reports
//!   itself available. In this build HTTPS is unavailable, so a configured
//!   provider is reported as configured-but-unusable instead of being silently
//!   ignored or faked. The fallback is stated in every response (`engine`,
//!   `engine_note`).
//!
//! API keys are never returned by any endpoint; only `key_set` is exposed.

use crate::domain::{Chunk, Source};
use crate::grounded::{self, Answer};
use crate::json::Value;
use crate::obj;
use std::path::PathBuf;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum ProviderKind {
    Extractive,
    OpenAiCompatible,
}

impl ProviderKind {
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ProviderKind::Extractive => "extractive",
            ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => "openai_compatible",
        }
    }
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<ProviderKind> {
        match s {
            "extractive" => Some(ProviderKind::Extractive),
            "openai_compatible" | "openai" | "byok" => Some(ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ProviderConfig {
    pub id: String,
    pub kind: String,
    pub base_url: String,
    pub model: String,
    pub created_at: String,
}

impl ProviderConfig {
    pub fn to_json(&self, key_set: bool) -> Value {
        obj! {
            "id" => self.id.as_str(),
            "kind" => self.kind.as_str(),
            "base_url" => self.base_url.as_str(),
            "model" => self.model.as_str(),
            "created_at" => self.created_at.as_str(),
            "key_set" => key_set,
            // Honest availability, computed rather than assumed.
            "available" => false,
            "reason" => "this build has no TLS client, so https providers cannot be contacted",
        }
    }
}

/// Validate user-supplied provider settings. https is mandatory: sending an API
/// key in cleartext is never acceptable, even to a "local" model.
pub fn validate(kind: &str, base_url: &str, model: &str, api_key: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let k = ProviderKind::parse(kind).ok_or_else(|| format!("unknown provider kind '{}'", kind))?;
    if k == ProviderKind::Extractive {
        return Ok(());
    }
    if !base_url.starts_with("https://") {
        return Err("base_url must start with https:// (refusing to send a key in cleartext)".into());
    }
    if base_url.len() > 512 {
        return Err("base_url is too long".into());
    }
    if model.trim().is_empty() {
        return Err("model name is required".into());
    }
    if api_key.trim().len() < 8 {
        return Err("api key looks too short".into());
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub trait Answerer {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn available(&self) -> bool;
    fn reason(&self) -> String;
    fn answer(&self, question: &str, chunks: &[Chunk], sources: &[Source], max: usize) -> Result<Answer, String>;
}

/// The default engine: composes an answer only from retrieved source sentences.
pub struct ExtractiveAnswerer;

impl Answerer for ExtractiveAnswerer {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
        "extractive"
    }
    fn available(&self) -> bool {
        true
    }
    fn reason(&self) -> String {
        "local extractive engine: answers are sentences quoted from your sources".into()
    }
    fn answer(&self, question: &str, chunks: &[Chunk], sources: &[Source], max: usize) -> Result<Answer, String> {
        Ok(grounded::answer(question, chunks, sources, max))
    }
}

/// Remote OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint. Kept behind the same trait so a
/// future build with TLS can switch engines without touching the API layer.
pub struct RemoteAnswerer {
    pub cfg: ProviderConfig,
    pub api_key: String,
}

impl Answerer for RemoteAnswerer {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
        "openai_compatible"
    }
    fn available(&self) -> bool {
        // Availability is a property of the build, not of the configuration.
        false
    }
    fn reason(&self) -> String {
        "provider configured, but this build cannot make TLS requests; using the local extractive engine".into()
    }
    fn answer(&self, _q: &str, _c: &[Chunk], _s: &[Source], _m: usize) -> Result<Answer, String> {
        Err("TLS/HTTPS is not available in this build; remote answering is impossible".into())
    }
}

/// Pick the engine to use. Never returns "none": there is always a local engine.
pub fn select(cfg: Option<&ProviderConfig>, key: Option<&str>) -> (Box<dyn Answerer>, String) {
    if let Some(c) = cfg {
        let remote = RemoteAnswerer { cfg: c.clone(), api_key: key.unwrap_or("").to_string() };
        if remote.available() {
            return (Box::new(remote), String::new());
        }
        let note = remote.reason();
        return (Box::new(ExtractiveAnswerer), note);
    }
    let e = ExtractiveAnswerer;
    (Box::new(e), String::new())
}

/// Secrets live outside the document database, with 0600 permissions.
pub fn secrets_path(data_dir: &std::path::Path) -> PathBuf {
    data_dir.join("secrets.json")
}

pub fn write_secret(data_dir: &std::path::Path, id: &str, key: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let path = secrets_path(data_dir);
    let mut map = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|s| crate::json::parse(&s).ok())
        .and_then(|v| match v {
            Value::Obj(m) => Some(m),
            _ => None,
        })
        .unwrap_or_default();
    map.insert(id.to_string(), Value::from(key));
    let tmp = path.with_extension("json.tmp");
    std::fs::write(&tmp, crate::json::to_string(&Value::Obj(map)))?;
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
        let _ = std::fs::set_permissions(&tmp, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600));
    }
    std::fs::rename(&tmp, &path)
}

pub fn read_secret(data_dir: &std::path::Path, id: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let s = std::fs::read_to_string(secrets_path(data_dir)).ok()?;
    let v = crate::json::parse(&s).ok()?;
    v.str_of(id).map(|x| x.to_string())
}

pub fn delete_secret(data_dir: &std::path::Path, id: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let path = secrets_path(data_dir);
    let s = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).ok()?;
    let mut v = crate::json::parse(&s).ok()?;
    let removed = v.str_of(id).map(|x| x.to_string());
    if removed.is_some() {
        if let Value::Obj(ref mut m) = v {
            m.remove(id);
        }
        let _ = std::fs::write(&path, crate::json::to_string(&v));
    }
    removed
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn rejects_cleartext_endpoints_and_short_keys() {
        assert!(validate("openai_compatible", "http://api.example.com", "gpt", "sk-12345678").is_err());
        assert!(validate("openai_compatible", "https://api.example.com", "", "sk-12345678").is_err());
        assert!(validate("openai_compatible", "https://api.example.com", "m", "short").is_err());
        assert!(validate("openai_compatible", "https://api.example.com", "m", "sk-12345678").is_ok());
        assert!(validate("magic", "https://x", "m", "sk-12345678").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn extractive_engine_is_always_selected() {
        let (a, note) = select(None, None);
        assert_eq!(a.name(), "extractive");
        assert!(a.available());
        assert!(note.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn configured_remote_provider_states_its_limitation() {
        let cfg = ProviderConfig {
            id: "p1".into(),
            kind: "openai_compatible".into(),
            base_url: "https://api.example.com".into(),
            model: "m".into(),
            created_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z".into(),
        };
        let (a, note) = select(Some(&cfg), Some("sk-12345678"));
        assert_eq!(a.name(), "extractive", "must fall back, never pretend");
        assert!(note.contains("TLS"));
        let json = cfg.to_json(true);
        assert_eq!(json.get("available").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()), Some(false));
        assert!(!crate::json::to_string(&json).contains("sk-12345678"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn secrets_are_private_and_removable() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("forge-secret-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        write_secret(&dir, "p1", "sk-secret-value").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(read_secret(&dir, "p1").as_deref(), Some("sk-secret-value"));
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
            let mode = std::fs::metadata(secrets_path(&dir)).unwrap().permissions().mode();
            assert_eq!(mode & 0o777, 0o600, "secrets file must be owner-only");
        }
        assert_eq!(delete_secret(&dir, "p1").as_deref(), Some("sk-secret-value"));
        assert!(read_secret(&dir, "p1").is_none());
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }
}

## `crates/forge-core/src/retrieve.rs`

```rust
//! Lexical retrieval (BM25) over evidence chunks.
//!
//! Lexical retrieval is the backbone, not a fallback: exact terms, identifiers,
//! names and numbers are precisely what embeddings blur. Semantic retrieval can
//! be added as a second ranker later (docs/FEATURE_BACKLOG.md) without changing
//! this contract.

use crate::domain::Chunk;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap, HashSet};

const K1: f64 = 1.2;
const B: f64 = 0.75;

pub const STOPWORDS: &[&str] = &[
    "a", "an", "and", "are", "as", "at", "be", "been", "but", "by", "for", "from", "has", "have",
    "how", "i", "in", "is", "it", "its", "of", "on", "or", "that", "the", "their", "then", "there",
    "these", "they", "this", "to", "was", "were", "what", "when", "where", "which", "who", "why",
    "will", "with", "you", "your", "do", "does", "did", "can", "could", "should", "would", "about",
    "into", "than", "so", "if", "we", "our", "us", "me", "my",
];

pub fn tokenize(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut cur = String::new();
    for ch in text.chars() {
        if ch.is_alphanumeric() {
            cur.extend(ch.to_lowercase());
        } else if !cur.is_empty() {
            out.push(std::mem::take(&mut cur));
        }
    }
    if !cur.is_empty() {
        out.push(cur);
    }
    out
}

/// Conservative suffix normaliser so "citation" matches "citations" and
/// "validated" matches "validate". Deliberately shallow: no dictionary, no
/// Porter stemmer, because over-stemming hurts precision on identifiers.
pub fn stem(term: &str) -> String {
    let t = term;
    if t.len() > 5 && t.ends_with("ies") {
        return format!("{}y", &t[..t.len() - 3]);
    }
    if t.len() > 5 && (t.ends_with("ses") || t.ends_with("xes") || t.ends_with("ches") || t.ends_with("shes") || t.ends_with("zes")) {
        return t[..t.len() - 2].to_string();
    }
    if t.len() > 3 && t.ends_with('s') && !t.ends_with("ss") && !t.ends_with("us") && !t.ends_with("is") {
        return t[..t.len() - 1].to_string();
    }
    if t.len() > 6 && t.ends_with("ing") {
        return t[..t.len() - 3].to_string();
    }
    if t.len() > 5 && t.ends_with("ed") {
        return t[..t.len() - 2].to_string();
    }
    t.to_string()
}

pub fn terms(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    tokenize(text)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|t| t.len() > 1 && !STOPWORDS.contains(&t.as_str()))
        .collect()
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Hit {
    pub chunk_index: usize,
    pub score: f64,
    pub matched_terms: Vec<String>,
}

/// BM25 over an in-memory chunk slice. Returns hits sorted by descending score.
pub fn search(chunks: &[Chunk], query: &str, limit: usize) -> Vec<Hit> {
    if chunks.is_empty() {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let q_terms: Vec<String> = {
        let mut seen = HashSet::new();
        terms(query)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|t| stem(&t))
            .filter(|t| seen.insert(t.clone()))
            .collect()
    };
    if q_terms.is_empty() {
        return Vec::new();
    }

    let docs: Vec<Vec<String>> = chunks
        .iter()
        .map(|c| tokenize(&c.text).iter().map(|t| stem(t)).collect())
        .collect();
    let n = docs.len() as f64;
    let avgdl = docs.iter().map(|d| d.len() as f64).sum::<f64>() / n;
    let avgdl = if avgdl <= 0.0 { 1.0 } else { avgdl };

    // document frequency per query term
    let mut df: HashMap<&str, usize> = HashMap::new();
    for t in &q_terms {
        let count = docs.iter().filter(|d| d.iter().any(|w| w == t)).count();
        df.insert(t.as_str(), count);
    }

    let mut hits = Vec::new();
    for (i, doc) in docs.iter().enumerate() {
        let dl = doc.len() as f64;
        let mut tf: BTreeMap<&str, usize> = BTreeMap::new();
        for w in doc {
            if let Some(t) = q_terms.iter().find(|t| *t == w) {
                *tf.entry(t.as_str()).or_insert(0) += 1;
            }
        }
        if tf.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let mut score = 0.0;
        let mut matched = Vec::new();
        for t in &q_terms {
            let f = *tf.get(t.as_str()).unwrap_or(&0) as f64;
            if f == 0.0 {
                continue;
            }
            let dfi = *df.get(t.as_str()).unwrap_or(&0) as f64;
            let idf = ((n - dfi + 0.5) / (dfi + 0.5) + 1.0).ln();
            let denom = f + K1 * (1.0 - B + B * dl / avgdl);
            score += idf * (f * (K1 + 1.0)) / denom;
            matched.push(t.clone());
        }
        // Exact phrase bonus: query appearing verbatim is strong evidence.
        if chunks[i].text.to_lowercase().contains(&query.trim().to_lowercase())
            && !query.trim().is_empty()
        {
            score *= 1.5;
        }
        hits.push(Hit { chunk_index: i, score, matched_terms: matched });
    }
    hits.sort_by(|a, b| b.score.partial_cmp(&a.score).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
    hits.truncate(limit);
    hits
}

/// Best-matching sentences from a passage, used to build precise quotes.
pub fn best_sentences(text: &str, query: &str, max: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    let q: HashSet<String> = terms(query).into_iter().collect();
    let mut sentences: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut cur = String::new();
    for ch in text.chars() {
        cur.push(ch);
        if matches!(ch, '.' | '!' | '?' | ';') {
            let t = cur.trim().to_string();
            if t.len() > 20 {
                sentences.push(t);
            }
            cur.clear();
        }
    }
    if cur.trim().len() > 20 {
        sentences.push(cur.trim().to_string());
    }
    if sentences.is_empty() {
        let t = text.trim();
        if !t.is_empty() {
            sentences.push(t.chars().take(400).collect());
        }
        return sentences;
    }
    let mut scored: Vec<(f64, String)> = sentences
        .into_iter()
        .map(|s| {
            let st: HashSet<String> = terms(&s).into_iter().collect();
            let overlap = q.intersection(&st).count() as f64 / (q.len().max(1) as f64);
            (overlap, s)
        })
        .collect();
    scored.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
    scored.into_iter().take(max).map(|(_, s)| s).collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::domain::Locator;

    fn chunk(id: &str, text: &str) -> Chunk {
        Chunk {
            id: id.into(),
            source_id: "s1".into(),
            notebook_id: "nb".into(),
            ordinal: 0,
            text: text.into(),
            locator: Locator::paragraph(0, 0, 1),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn ranks_the_relevant_chunk_first() {
        let chunks = vec![
            chunk("a", "The weather in Kerala is humid during the monsoon season."),
            chunk("b", "Forge validates every citation against an indexed evidence span."),
            chunk("c", "Unrelated text about gardening and soil."),
        ];
        let hits = search(&chunks, "citation evidence span", 3);
        assert!(!hits.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(chunks[hits[0].chunk_index].id, "b");
        assert!(hits[0].score > 0.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn exact_identifiers_are_found() {
        let chunks = vec![
            chunk("a", "The configuration key is FORGE_DATA_DIR and it controls storage."),
            chunk("b", "Something else entirely about storage of grain."),
        ];
        let hits = search(&chunks, "FORGE_DATA_DIR", 2);
        assert_eq!(chunks[hits[0].chunk_index].id, "a");
    }

    #[test]
    fn no_match_returns_empty() {
        let chunks = vec![chunk("a", "apples and oranges")];
        assert!(search(&chunks, "kubernetes ingress", 5).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn stopword_only_query_returns_nothing() {
        let chunks = vec![chunk("a", "the quick brown fox")];
        assert!(search(&chunks, "the of and to", 5).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn sentence_selection_prefers_overlap() {
        let text = "The sky is blue. Forge citations point at exact evidence spans. \
                    Bananas are yellow.";
        let best = best_sentences(text, "where do citations point", 1);
        assert_eq!(best.len(), 1);
        assert!(best[0].contains("citations"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn tokenizer_handles_unicode_and_punctuation() {
        let t = tokenize("Café, naïve — 42% done");
        assert!(t.contains(&"café".to_string()));
        assert!(t.contains(&"42".to_string()));
    }
}

## `crates/forge-core/src/security.rs`

```rust
//! Security helpers: URL/SSRF policy, path safety, size limits, output escaping.

use std::net::{IpAddr, ToSocketAddrs};

pub const MAX_SOURCE_BYTES: usize = 25 * 1024 * 1024;
pub const MAX_TEXT_BYTES: usize = 8 * 1024 * 1024;
pub const MAX_URL_LEN: usize = 2048;

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum UrlVerdict {
    Allowed(String),
    Rejected(String),
}

/// Validate a URL for ingestion.
///
/// Policy: only http/https; never localhost, link-local, private, CGNAT,
/// multicast or unspecified addresses; hostnames are resolved and ALL resolved
/// addresses must be public (defeats DNS-rebinding to an internal service).
pub fn check_url(raw: &str) -> UrlVerdict {
    let raw = raw.trim();
    if raw.is_empty() {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected("empty url".into());
    }
    if raw.len() > MAX_URL_LEN {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected("url too long".into());
    }
    let lower = raw.to_ascii_lowercase();
    let (scheme, rest) = match lower.split_once("://") {
        Some(v) => v,
        None => return UrlVerdict::Rejected("missing scheme (http/https)".into()),
    };
    if scheme != "http" && scheme != "https" {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected(format!("scheme '{}' is not allowed", scheme));
    }
    let authority = rest.split(['/', '?', '#']).next().unwrap_or("");
    if authority.is_empty() {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected("missing host".into());
    }
    let host_port = authority.rsplit('@').next().unwrap_or(authority); // strip userinfo
    let host = if host_port.starts_with('[') {
        // IPv6 literal
        host_port
            .split(']')
            .next()
            .unwrap_or("")
            .trim_start_matches('[')
            .to_string()
    } else {
        host_port.split(':').next().unwrap_or("").to_string()
    };
    if host.is_empty() {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected("missing host".into());
    }
    let host_lower = host.to_ascii_lowercase();
    if host_lower == "localhost" || host_lower.ends_with(".localhost") || host_lower.ends_with(".local") {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected("localhost/.local hosts are blocked".into());
    }
    if host_lower == "metadata" || host_lower.contains("metadata.google.internal") {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected("cloud metadata hosts are blocked".into());
    }
    if let Ok(ip) = host_lower.parse::<IpAddr>() {
        if !is_public_ip(&ip) {
            return UrlVerdict::Rejected(format!("address {} is not public", ip));
        }
        return UrlVerdict::Allowed(lower);
    }
    // resolve and check every address
    match (host_lower.as_str(), 80u16).to_socket_addrs() {
        Ok(addrs) => {
            let ips: Vec<IpAddr> = addrs.map(|a| a.ip()).collect();
            if ips.is_empty() {
                return UrlVerdict::Rejected("host did not resolve".into());
            }
            for ip in ips {
                if !is_public_ip(&ip) {
                    return UrlVerdict::Rejected(format!(
                        "host resolves to non-public address {}",
                        ip
                    ));
                }
            }
            UrlVerdict::Allowed(lower)
        }
        Err(e) => UrlVerdict::Rejected(format!("dns resolution failed: {}", e)),
    }
}

pub fn is_public_ip(ip: &IpAddr) -> bool {
    match ip {
        IpAddr::V4(v4) => {
            let o = v4.octets();
            !(v4.is_private()
                || v4.is_loopback()
                || v4.is_link_local()
                || v4.is_broadcast()
                || v4.is_multicast()
                || v4.is_unspecified()
                || (o[0] == 100 && (64..=127).contains(&o[1])) // CGNAT 100.64/10
                || (o[0] == 169 && o[1] == 254) // link-local / metadata
                || o[0] == 0)
        }
        IpAddr::V6(v6) => {
            !(v6.is_loopback()
                || v6.is_unspecified()
                || v6.is_multicast()
                || (v6.segments()[0] & 0xfe00) == 0xfc00 // unique local
                || (v6.segments()[0] & 0xffc0) == 0xfe80) // link local
        }
    }
}

/// Resolve a name inside a root directory, refusing traversal and absolute paths.
pub fn safe_join(root: &std::path::Path, rel: &str) -> Option<std::path::PathBuf> {
    if rel.contains('\0') {
        return None;
    }
    let cleaned = rel.trim_start_matches('/');
    let mut out = root.to_path_buf();
    for part in cleaned.split('/') {
        if part.is_empty() || part == "." {
            continue;
        }
        if part == ".." || part.contains('\\') || part.contains(':') {
            return None;
        }
        out.push(part);
    }
    // canonicalise to be sure (the target must exist for this check)
    let canon = out.canonicalize().ok()?;
    let root_canon = root.canonicalize().ok()?;
    if canon.starts_with(&root_canon) {
        Some(canon)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

pub fn escape_html(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    for c in s.chars() {
        match c {
            '<' => out.push_str("&lt;"),
            '>' => out.push_str("&gt;"),
            '&' => out.push_str("&amp;"),
            '"' => out.push_str("&quot;"),
            '\'' => out.push_str("&#39;"),
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Restrict an uploaded filename to something safe for display only.
pub fn clean_filename(name: &str) -> String {
    let base = name.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or(name);
    let cleaned: String = base
        .chars()
        .filter(|c| c.is_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '.' | '-' | '_' | ' ' | '(' | ')'))
        .take(120)
        .collect();
    if cleaned.trim().is_empty() {
        "upload".to_string()
    } else {
        cleaned
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn blocks_ssrf_targets() {
        for bad in [
            "http://localhost/admin",
            "http://127.0.0.1:8080/",
            "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/",
            "http://10.0.0.5/",
            "http://192.168.1.1/",
            "http://[::1]/",
            "http://100.64.1.1/",
            "ftp://example.com/x",
            "file:///etc/passwd",
            "http://metadata.google.internal/",
            "not-a-url",
        ] {
            assert!(
                matches!(check_url(bad), UrlVerdict::Rejected(_)),
                "should reject {}",
                bad
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn allows_public_http() {
        // 93.184.216.34 is a public address; no DNS needed for the literal.
        assert!(matches!(check_url("http://93.184.216.34/page"), UrlVerdict::Allowed(_)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn ip_classification() {
        assert!(!is_public_ip(&"127.0.0.1".parse().unwrap()));
        assert!(!is_public_ip(&"10.1.2.3".parse().unwrap()));
        assert!(!is_public_ip(&"172.16.0.1".parse().unwrap()));
        assert!(is_public_ip(&"8.8.8.8".parse().unwrap()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn path_traversal_is_refused() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("forge-sec-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(root.join("ok.txt"), b"x").unwrap();
        assert!(safe_join(&root, "ok.txt").is_some());
        assert!(safe_join(&root, "../etc/passwd").is_none());
        assert!(safe_join(&root, "/etc/passwd").is_none());
        assert!(safe_join(&root, "a/../../etc/passwd").is_none());
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&root).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn html_escaping_prevents_markup() {
        assert_eq!(escape_html("<script>x</script>"), "&lt;script&gt;x&lt;/script&gt;");
    }

    #[test]
    fn filenames_are_sanitised() {
        assert_eq!(clean_filename("../../etc/passwd"), "passwd");
        assert_eq!(clean_filename("a/b/c.pdf"), "c.pdf");
        assert_eq!(clean_filename(""), "upload");
    }
}

## `crates/forge-core/src/store.rs`

```rust
//! Durable state: an in-memory `Db` written through to JSON on disk.
//!
//! Why not SQLite: crates.io is unreachable (docs/DECISIONS.md D1), and the
//! Rust standard library has no database. A single JSON document with atomic
//! replace (write temp + rename) is what we can verify end-to-end. See
//! docs/DECISIONS.md D2 for the scale limit this implies.

use crate::domain::*;
use crate::json::{self, Value};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Mutex;

#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct Db {
    pub notebooks: Vec<Notebook>,
    pub sources: Vec<Source>,
    pub chunks: Vec<Chunk>,
    pub conversations: Vec<Conversation>,
    pub notes: Vec<Note>,
    pub artifacts: Vec<Artifact>,
}

pub struct Store {
    pub dir: PathBuf,
    inner: Mutex<Db>,
}

impl Store {
    pub fn open(dir: impl AsRef<Path>) -> std::io::Result<Store> {
        let dir = dir.as_ref().to_path_buf();
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir)?;
        fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("backups"))?;
        let db = match fs::read_to_string(dir.join("db.json")) {
            Ok(text) => decode_db(&text).unwrap_or_default(),
            Err(_) => Db::default(),
        };
        let s = Store { dir, inner: Mutex::new(db) };
        if !s.path().exists() {
            s.save()?;
        }
        Ok(s)
    }

    pub fn path(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.dir.join("db.json")
    }

    pub fn read<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&Db) -> R) -> R {
        let guard = self.inner.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        f(&guard)
    }

    /// Mutate + persist. The write is atomic (tmp + rename) so a crash cannot
    /// leave a half-written database.
    pub fn write<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Db) -> R) -> std::io::Result<R> {
        let mut guard = self.inner.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        let out = f(&mut guard);
        let text = json::to_pretty(&encode_db(&guard));
        let tmp = self.dir.join("db.json.tmp");
        fs::write(&tmp, text.as_bytes())?;
        fs::rename(&tmp, self.path())?;
        Ok(out)
    }

    pub fn save(&self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        self.write(|_| ())
    }

    /// Rolling backup used by the export/backup workflow and manual recovery.
    pub fn backup(&self) -> std::io::Result<PathBuf> {
        let name = format!("backups/db-{}.json", now_iso().replace([':', 'T', 'Z'], "-"));
        let dest = self.dir.join(&name);
        let text = self.read(|db| json::to_pretty(&encode_db(db)));
        fs::write(&dest, text.as_bytes())?;
        Ok(dest)
    }
}

fn encode_db(db: &Db) -> Value {
    let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
    m.insert("schema".into(), Value::from("forge.db/1"));
    m.insert("notebooks".into(), Value::Arr(db.notebooks.iter().map(nb_json).collect()));
    m.insert("sources".into(), Value::Arr(db.sources.iter().map(source_json).collect()));
    m.insert("chunks".into(), Value::Arr(db.chunks.iter().map(chunk_json).collect()));
    m.insert(
        "conversations".into(),
        Value::Arr(db.conversations.iter().map(conv_json).collect()),
    );
    m.insert("notes".into(), Value::Arr(db.notes.iter().map(note_json).collect()));
    m.insert("artifacts".into(), Value::Arr(db.artifacts.iter().map(artifact_json).collect()));
    Value::Obj(m)
}

fn decode_db(text: &str) -> Option<Db> {
    let v = json::parse(text).ok()?;
    let arr = |key: &str| v.get(key).and_then(|x| x.as_arr()).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    Some(Db {
        notebooks: arr("notebooks").iter().map(nb_from).collect(),
        sources: arr("sources").iter().map(source_from).collect(),
        chunks: arr("chunks").iter().map(chunk_from).collect(),
        conversations: arr("conversations").iter().map(conv_from).collect(),
        notes: arr("notes").iter().map(note_from).collect(),
        artifacts: arr("artifacts").iter().map(artifact_from).collect(),
    })
}

fn nb_json(n: &Notebook) -> Value {
    let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
    m.insert("id".into(), Value::from(n.id.as_str()));
    m.insert("title".into(), Value::from(n.title.as_str()));
    m.insert("description".into(), Value::from(n.description.as_str()));
    m.insert("instructions".into(), Value::from(n.instructions.as_str()));
    m.insert("tags".into(), json_str_list(&n.tags));
    m.insert("archived".into(), Value::Bool(n.archived));
    m.insert("created_at".into(), Value::from(n.created_at.as_str()));
    m.insert("updated_at".into(), Value::from(n.updated_at.as_str()));
    Value::Obj(m)
}

fn nb_from(v: &Value) -> Notebook {
    Notebook {
        id: s(v, "id"),
        title: s(v, "title"),
        description: s(v, "description"),
        instructions: s(v, "instructions"),
        tags: parse_str_list(v.get("tags")),
        archived: v.get("archived").and_then(|b| b.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false),
        created_at: s(v, "created_at"),
        updated_at: s(v, "updated_at"),
    }
}

}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn tmpdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let p = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("forge-test-{}-{}", tag, new_id("t")));
        fs::create_dir_all(&p).unwrap();
        p
    }

    #[test]
    fn persists_across_reopen() {
        let dir = tmpdir("persist");
        {
            let st = Store::open(&dir).unwrap();
            st.write(|db| {
                db.notebooks.push(Notebook {
                    id: "nb-1".into(),
                    title: "Research".into(),
                    description: String::new(),
                    instructions: String::new(),
                    tags: vec!["x".into()],
                    archived: false,
                    created_at: now_iso(),
                    updated_at: now_iso(),
                });
            })
            .unwrap();
        }
        let st2 = Store::open(&dir).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(st2.read(|db| db.notebooks.len()), 1);
        assert_eq!(st2.read(|db| db.notebooks[0].title.clone()), "Research");
        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn atomic_write_leaves_no_tmp_file() {
        let dir = tmpdir("atomic");
        let st = Store::open(&dir).unwrap();
        st.write(|db| db.notebooks.clear()).unwrap();
        assert!(!dir.join("db.json.tmp").exists());
        assert!(dir.join("db.json").exists());
        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn corrupt_db_does_not_panic() {
        let dir = tmpdir("corrupt");
        fs::write(dir.join("db.json"), "{not json").unwrap();
        let st = Store::open(&dir).unwrap(); // falls back to empty
        assert_eq!(st.read(|db| db.notebooks.len()), 0);
        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn backup_writes_a_copy() {
        let dir = tmpdir("backup");
        let st = Store::open(&dir).unwrap();
        let p = st.backup().unwrap();
        assert!(p.exists());
        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }
}

## `crates/forge-core/src/web.rs`

```rust
//! Static hosting for the single-page web app.
//!
//! Serves files only from inside the configured web root (path traversal is
//! refused) and falls back to `index.html` for client-side routes.

use crate::http::{mime_for, Response};
use crate::obj;
use crate::security::safe_join;
use std::path::Path;

pub fn serve_static(root: &Path, path: &str) -> Response {
    let rel = if path == "/" || path.is_empty() {
        "index.html".to_string()
    } else {
        path.trim_start_matches('/').to_string()
    };

    if let Some(full) = safe_join(root, &rel) {
        if full.is_file() {
            return match std::fs::read(&full) {
                Ok(bytes) => {
                    let mut res = Response::new(200, mime_for(&rel), bytes);
                    res = res.with_header("Cache-Control", "no-cache");
                    res
                }
                Err(_) => Response::text(500, "read error"),
            };
        }
    }

    // Client-side routing: extension-less unknown paths get the app shell.
    if !rel.contains('.') {
        if let Some(index) = safe_join(root, "index.html") {
            if let Ok(bytes) = std::fs::read(&index) {
                return Response::new(200, "text/html; charset=utf-8", bytes);
            }
        }
    }

    Response::json(404, &obj! { "error" => "not found", "code" => "static_404" })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn app_dir() -> std::path::PathBuf {
        std::path::PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../apps/web")
    }

    #[test]
    fn serves_the_shell_and_assets() {
        let root = app_dir();
        let index = serve_static(&root, "/");
        assert_eq!(index.status, 200);
        assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&index.body).contains("Forge"));
        assert_eq!(serve_static(&root, "/app.js").status, 200);
        assert_eq!(serve_static(&root, "/styles.css").content_type, "text/css; charset=utf-8");
    }

    #[test]
    fn deep_links_fall_back_to_shell() {
        let r = serve_static(&app_dir(), "/nb/abc123");
        assert_eq!(r.status, 200);
        assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&r.body).contains("app.js"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn traversal_and_missing_assets_are_refused() {
        let root = app_dir();
        for p in ["/../Cargo.toml", "/../../etc/passwd", "/%2e%2e/Cargo.toml"] {
            let r = serve_static(&root, p);
            assert_ne!(r.status, 200, "must not serve {}", p);
        }
        let missing = serve_static(&root, "/nope.js");
        assert_eq!(missing.status, 404);
    }
}
